_meta.title: RCSA calculation truth table — SB_RCSA Template 2026
_meta.purpose: The shared fixture for App\Services\Rcsa\RcsaCalculationService (PHP) and resources/js/lib/rcsa-calc.js (browser). Both are run over every case by tests/Unit/Rcsa/RcsaCalculationTest, so the client mirror cannot drift from the server engine.
_meta.derivation: Written from section 3.3 of the RCSA Module Implementation Plan, independently of either implementation, so that the test compares two readings of the spec rather than one implementation with itself. VERIFIED against the workbook itself on 2026-09-07: all 100 cases (5 likelihood x 5 impact x 4 control effectiveness) reproduce the formulas in 'plans/SB _RCSA Template 2026 - Template.xlsx', RCSA Sheet row 3, exactly. tests/Unit/Rcsa/RcsaWorkbookParityTest re-derives them from the transcribed formulas on every run.

formulas.band: s <= 2 very_low; s <= 4 low; s <= 9 medium; s <= 16 high; else very_high
formulas.ceModifier: Fully Achieved 100; Mostly Achieved 75; Partially Achieved 50; Not Achieved 25
formulas.riskTreatment: {very_high, high} treat; medium mitigate; {low, very_low} accept

workbookFormulas.source: plans/SB _RCSA Template 2026 - Template.xlsx, sheet 'RCSA Sheet', row 3
workbookFormulas.R_residualLevel: same bands as M, applied to Q
workbookFormulas.T_appetite: =IF(S3="ACCEPT","Within risk appetite: Continue routine monitoring",IF(S3="MITIGATE","Above risk appetite:mitigate",IF(S3="TREAT","Above risk appetite:Treat")))
workbookFormulas.note: The workbook contradicts itself in two places and the FORMULA wins, because the formula is what calculates. Its Risk Matrix sheet calls impact level 3 'Moderate' while the L formula matches on 'Medium'; its Control effectiveness grid spells the ratings lower-case ('Fully achieved') while the P formula matches on 'Fully Achieved'.
